newsitem.title: UK: UNITED NEWS SET TO BID FOR BLENHEIM - REPORT.
newsitem.headline: UNITED NEWS SET TO BID FOR BLENHEIM - REPORT.

text.p: Britain's United News & Media is set to table a 480 million stg bid for exhibitions group Blenheim , the Sunday Telegraph reported.

The report said that United's advisers had held weekend meetings with merchant bank Kleinwort Benson to discuss the situation. It said United was likely to offer 520p a share for Blenheim, valuing the company at 480 million stg.
Blenheim shares closed on Friday at 485p.
United News and Anglo-Dutch group Reed-Elsevier , have long been seen as rival suitors for Blenheim.
But Dutch publisher VNU took them by surprise last week when it paid institutional investors 500p per share to build a 15 percent stake.
VNU has called the move a strategic long-term investment and said it had no intention of making an offer for Blenheim, barring rival offers for the firm.
The Sunday Telegraph report said VNU's move had prompted Reed to drop out of negotiations. But it said a bidding war now loomed between United News and VNU.
Media group United, which merged with television and financial services group MAI earlier this year, wants Blenheim to expand its Miller Freeman exhibitions arm.
None of the companies involved were immediately available for an immediatte comment.
